summary: Add new KV cache fragmentation/compaction runtime metrics to central telemetry schema + ensure retention in observability pipeline
description:
Request:
We need to register new Serving Runtime KV-cache metrics in the central telemetry schema so they are accepted by the ingestion pipeline, queryable in standard tooling, and retained at the required resolution for canary + incident response.

Background:
Runtime team is shipping KV cache compaction/eviction changes behind a flag. They added fragmentation + compaction counters in runtime structured telemetry (see related PR), and SRE/Obs is building alerts/dashboards. Currently these metric names are showing up as "unknown metric" / dropped in some environments because they are not in the central schema allowlist.

Why this matters:
- Canary rollout gating depends on p99 and allocator failure rate correlated with fragmentation signals.
- Incident response needs short-term high-resolution retention (at least 7d) to diagnose spikes and support tickets.
- Longer-term trendline retention (>= 30d) needed to validate compaction tuning per pool.

Requested metrics (proposed names + types):
1) runtime.kv_cache.fragmentation_ratio (gauge)
   - Definition: 1 - (largest_free_contiguous_bytes / total_free_bytes) OR equivalent allocator-defined fragmentation metric
   - Units: ratio [0..1]
2) runtime.kv_cache.alloc_failures_total (counter)
   - Definition: allocation failures in KV cache allocator (includes retry/slow-path) labeled by failure_class
3) runtime.kv_cache.evictions_total (counter)
   - Definition: sequences/pages evicted to satisfy allocation pressure
4) runtime.kv_cache.compaction.bytes_moved_total (counter)
   - Definition: total bytes moved by compaction engine
5) runtime.kv_cache.compaction.events_total (counter)
   - Definition: compaction runs (budget cycle) by trigger_type
6) runtime.kv_cache.compaction.time_ms (histogram)
   - Definition: time spent compacting per event; must be usable to attribute compaction overhead to tail latency

Required labels/tags:
- region (low cardinality)
- pool (bounded set; hosted pool names + dedicated pool id)
- model_family (bounded taxonomy; e.g., llama, mistral, qwen)
- tenant_tier (hosted|dedicated|private OR self_serve|dedicated|private; whichever is standard)
- trigger_type (threshold|allocation_failure|interval)
- failure_class (oom|fragmentation|budget|other)

Cardinality constraints (IMPORTANT):
- Please do NOT accept raw model_id, request_id, customer_id, or pod_id as labels.
- pool should be normalized (bounded). If dedicated pool ids are too high-card, we can map to "dedicated" + pool_name or "dedicated:<hash_bucket>" (please advise).

Retention requirements:
- High-resolution (10s-60s scrape) for 7 days minimum (needed for canary + incident triage).
- 5m downsampled for 30 days minimum.
- 1h downsampled for 13 months (if available in the standard pipeline) for long-term regressions.

Acceptance criteria:
- Metrics are added to central telemetry schema and are no longer dropped.
- Metrics are visible in the standard query layer used by dashboards/alerts.
- Retention policy is confirmed in writing (what we get at raw vs downsampled).
- A short note is added to the internal metrics catalog / naming doc indicating definitions + units.

References:
- Runtime PR adding metrics + structured logs: sources/github/redwood/pr-18423.json
- Dashboard/alerts PR consuming metrics: sources/github/observability-pack/pr-521.json
- Runtime architecture page w/ metric definitions: sources/confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runtime-architecture/kv-cache-allocator-and-fragmentation-metrics.json

Owner request:
Please coordinate w/ Logan Wright for schema changes + any ingestion constraints; loop in Sean Gallagher (SRE) for canary readiness if retention constraints require changing alert windows.
